subject: Clarify billing quantum and context billing for Acme PoC
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify billing quantum & context billing for PoC

Hi Soojin,

Quick question from procurement as we're drafting the PoC SOW: your pricing doc references a "billing quantum" and a few different rounding rules for context vs. generation tokens. For our cost projections we need concrete examples so we can map expected monthly charges to our internal forecast. Two specific asks:

- If we send a single request with a 1,700-token prompt and ask for a 500-token completion, how will the request be metered/rounded?
- For streaming/long conversation use (we plan to keep a 40k-token context bucket across many short requests), how is context maintained and billed? Is there a per-request minimum, a monthly minimum, or chunking that could inflate costs?

We're also trying to finalize the minimum commit for the Dedicated trial. If there are any waivers or first-month adjustments you can make while we validate throughput, please let me know so procurement can reflect it in the SOW.

Appreciate a short worked example and any pro-forma numbers.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
Head of ML Infrastructure, Acme Analytics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing quantum & context billing for PoC

Hi Samir — great questions, thanks for the concrete scenarios. Short version up-front, followed by worked examples.

High level (how we show up on invoices):
- Metering granularity: we technically record usage per token (1-token granularity), but for billing simplicity we apply a billing quantum that groups small requests into predictable buckets.
- Two quanta: "context quantum" and "generation quantum." Context (input / KV cache) is billed in blocks; generation (model output) is billed in smaller blocks.
- Minimums: hosted API has a per-request floor for micro-requests; Dedicated contracts may include a monthly commit that acts as a floor but can be adjusted for PoC.

Worked examples (your numbers):
1) Single request: 1,700-token prompt + 500-token completion
   - Context: we bill context in 512-token blocks. 1,700 rounded up -> 2 x 512 = 1024, but because 1,700 > 1024, it becomes 4 x 512 = 2048 tokens billed as context.
   - Generation: billed in 64-token quanta. 500 rounded up -> 8 x 64 = 512 tokens billed as generation.
   - Invoice line items: context 2,048 tokens @ context rate; generation 512 tokens @ generation rate.

2) Long conversation (40k token rolling context across many short requests)
   - We persist the KV cache and charge context once per snapshot refresh. Internally we use a 'context snapshot' cadence (default hourly for long-lived sessions) that results in periodic context charges in 512-token blocks per snapshot.
   - For your 40k working set that would be ~78 blocks of 512 (40,000 / 512 ≈ 78.1) billed each snapshot. If many short requests reuse that snapshot within the cadence, you avoid repeated context charges.

3) Minimums & rounding effects on small bursts
   - For Hosted API we have a per-request floor of 128 tokens billed (applies when requests are tiny). For Dedicated/committed customers we can roll that into the monthly commit and show net effective unit pricing.

PoC concession: we're happy to waive the first-month minimum (up to the agreed committed amount) for your Dedicated trial so you can validate throughput before the floor applies. We'll put this in the SOW if procurement wants it.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with pro-forma numbers at a few utilization levels. Happy to walk through live if helpful.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify billing quantum & context billing for PoC

Rishi / Marissa — forwarding Samir's procurement questions and my reply (below). Two quick operational asks before I send the formal SOW:

1) Can billing systems represent the "context billed in 512-token blocks" language cleanly on the invoice, or do we need to present it as "rounded to nearest 512 token equivalent"? Marissa, will that produce any rounding disputes?

2) I'm proposing we offer Acme a one-time concession: waive first-month committed-floor up to their trial cap (they're aiming for a 2-week Dedicated trial, estimated 120k tokens/day peak). I'll include language in the SOW but want to confirm finance ok with a waiver for the first billing period. Rishi, any objections on commercial?

Marissa replied inline: 

> Soojin — billing engine supports arbitrary per-token accounting (we write by token), invoices already present separate context/generation lines. The only operational gotcha: our downstream billing export aggregates to daily buckets and uses integers; recommending we phrase externally as "context billed in 512-token increments" to avoid confusion. I can add a short note to invoices that explains the rounding example.

> On the waiver: finance typically approves first-month waivers for PoC if deal owner confirms expected ARR uplift. If you can capture a commitment term after PoC (e.g., 6–12 month committed capacity), they will sign off.

I'll wait 1–2 hours for any pushback, then send a formal email to Samir with the SOW and a line about the first-month waiver.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing quantum & context billing for PoC

Hi Samir — quick follow-up with what we'll put in the SOW and an operational note.

1) Metering language we'll include in the SOW (short form):
   - Context billed in 512-token increments (round up).
   - Generation billed in 64-token increments (round up).
   - Small requests may be subject to a 128-token per-request floor on Hosted; Dedicated customers' floors are handled via monthly commit.

2) PoC concession: Redwood will waive the first-month minimum commitment up to the trial cap (two-week Dedicated trial sized at your requested throughput). This waiver will be documented in the SOW. Post-PoC, we will reconvene to agree on committed capacity; typical finance requirement is a 6–12 month commit for continued waiver/discounts.

3) Operational note for cost projections (we've attached acme-usage-estimate.xlsx demonstrating nominal monthly lines for three utilization profiles). The attachment includes the worked example from my original reply so you can paste numbers into your internal forecast.

Next steps: I'll attach an updated SOW (Acme-PoC-SOW-draft.pdf) with the waiver language. If procurement is happy, sign and return and we'll start scheduling Dedicated capacity. If you'd like, I can set up a 30-minute call with Marissa to walk through the invoice examples.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Acme-PoC-SOW-draft.pdf (PDF), acme-usage-estimate.xlsx (Excel)
